text:
maya (support): User reports p99 latency spike in ap-south models after last weekend's infra rollouts. They see 4x p99 and some 500s. Can oncall grab?

olivia (oncall): looking now, any customer IDs or request ids?

maya (support): sent customer id + sample request in DM. snippet: `req_id=8f9c3a model=gpt-open-13b seq=1024` — errors are timeouts and 502s.

olivia (oncall): seeing elevated p99 on ap-south hosts, correlates with CUDA 12.3 driver push on Sat night. p95 also up but less.

leo (infra): rolling driver/firmware timeline: CUDA driver pushed 02:00 UTC Sat, GPU FW patch 03:10 UTC, host kernel security backport 04:30 UTC. Storage qdepth spiked around 05:00 UTC.

sam (eng-runtime): interesting — logs show frequent NVMe queue stalls and long stall durations inside our batched inference loop. KV cache flushes spike at the same time.

carla (sre): can we repro on a small node? I'll try to repro with a synthetic workload that mimics long sequences + dense batching.

sam (eng-runtime): repro steps I've used locally:
```
# synth load
python perf/load.py --model gpt-open-13b --seq 1024 --concurrency 24 --profile
# watch iostat
iostat -x 1
```
When I ramp concurrency to ~20, NVMe await jumps and tail latency shoots up.

leo (infra): quick mitigation options: 1) rollback CUDA driver on small subset, 2) isolate noisy VMs to separate storage pools, 3) temporarily reduce batch size / force sync-less inference. Which should we try first?

olivia (oncall): prioritize customer impact -> route high-SLO customers off problematic hosts and enable fallback model variant (smaller quantized) for affected regions. Sam, can runtime enable model variant fallback?

sam (eng-runtime): yes, I can push a soft-fallback rule to route to 13b-8q if p99 > 1s for 3m. Preparing change now.

carla (sre): I'll add a flag to isolate host-level IO by adjusting cgroup io.weight for background jobs and throttle snapshot jobs. That should reduce host contention.

leo (infra): starting a targeted rollback of the CUDA driver on two suspect hosts and moving their instances into maintenance. Will report back in 10m.

deploy-bot: Rollout: cuda-driver-12.3 -> rollback initiated on hosts gpu-ap-12, gpu-ap-17 by leo at 1754020020.

maya (support): updated customer with workaround: enabling fallback to smaller model and moving traffic. They acknowledged, appreciate fast response.

sam (eng-runtime): fallback rule deployed to ap-south: if backend p99 > 1000ms then route to 13b-8q (graceful). Observed immediate drop in user-facing p99 for samples.

carla (sre): adjusted io.weight and paused nightly snapshot jobs on affected hosts — IOPS contention visibly reduced. iostat shows await down from ~40ms to ~6ms.

leo (infra): rollback completed on gpu-ap-12 and gpu-ap-17. Those hosts show kernel logs free of nvme stalls so far. I'll keep them in maintenance until we validate for 30m.

olivia (oncall): initial verdict: combination of driver + kernel backport + heavy KV-cache flushes triggered NVMe queue-depth storms for specific workload patterns. Mitigations applied: traffic routing to fallback model, driver rollback on hot hosts, cgroup IO throttling, pause snapshot jobs.

sam (eng-runtime): follow-ups: add conservative batch size cap per-host when storage await > 10ms, and a runtime gauge to track KV cache flush rate tied to IO. I'll open an RFC for config default changes.

carla (sre): also recommend build a canary for future driver/fw pushes that includes a synthetic long-seq NVMe-heavy workload. We missed this pattern in rollout tests.

leo (infra): agreed. I'll also coordinate with cloud partner to get NVMe firmware checks and look for drive SMART anomalies.

maya (support): customer confirmed decreased errors and p99 back to acceptable for their traffic. I'll keep channel updated if they see regression. :thumbsup:

olivia (oncall): moving to postmortem tracking — create incident doc and assign action items: rollbacks, canary tests, runtime fallback defaults, and snapshot schedule changes.

sam (eng-runtime): created issue INF-1327 for runtime defaults + telemetry.

carla (sre): created issue SRE-894 for canary and IO throttle automation.

leo (infra): created infra ticket INFRA-451 for driver/firmware rollout gating and SMART scanning.

maya (support): thanks everyone, closing loop with customer.
